metadata.title: The cli-explainer Skill.
metadata.note: cli-explainer skill teardown for the @HumanitariansAI Brutalist playlist (episode 06). The reel USES the ai-explainer skill-teardown modifier applied to cli-explainer's own SKILL.md. Every on-screen quote is from the file at that hash; every command shown in the demo/ log ran against the isolated toolkit copy. The isolated toolkit's ClaudeTitleOutro carries a handle prop so the outro reads @HumanitariansAI instead of the hardcoded @NikBearBrown of the public library; the BrutalistHesitantWriter scale is patched portrait-aware; four native 916 compositions were registered in Root.tsx. See SOURCES.md.

beats.act: ANATOMY — a skill is a folder
beats.role_note: SkillTeardownAnatomy — the SKILL.md file structure inside skills/make/cli-explainer/
beats.narration_text: A skill in this toolkit is a folder. Two files sit under skills-slash-make-slash-cli-explainer. SKILL dot m-d, three hundred sixty-five lines of plain markdown, and a reference directory with one example beat sheet. That is the whole skill. No compiled binary, no daemon, no service. Claude reads the file, and the file writes the reel.

beats.role_note: SkillTeardownPipeline — the CLI-video required beat spine, verbatim structure from SKILL.md §'The required beat spine'
beats.narration_text: The file is not a suggestion. It fixes the shape of every CLI reel to a nine-step spine. Cold open, problem, ask, code, output, revision, code again, better output, summary, hand-off, outro. Same in every reel. The creative work happens inside the frame. The frame itself is locked.

show.event: eyebrow + title 'The required beat spine.' land
INPUT node → each phase draws itself in narration order → OUTPUT node
footer note settles under the spine

beats.role_note: ClaudeComposerAsk — inner beat, command already typed. The ACTUAL invocation for THIS skill teardown.
beats.narration_text: The ask, verbatim from the file's own trigger table. c-l-i, followed by the concept. No model version, no temperature. The trigger tells Claude which skill to load. The skin defaults to Claude. The persona defaults to Liam. This is the only entry point.

show.event: composer already shows the typed trigger (no re-typing — inner beat)

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the ACTUAL SKILL.md excerpt that owns THIS reel's structure
beats.narration_text: This is the section that owns the video you are watching. Mandatory in the sixteen-by-nine cut. One, the problem beat. Two, at least one revision cycle. Three, the summary and next steps before the outro. A CLI video without a check-and-change is incomplete. That is a rule in the skill, not a note in a review.

show.event: code card fades in; filename tab reads 'SKILL.md § required spine'

props.title: skills/make/cli-explainer/SKILL.md
props.code:
# § The required beat spine

# Mandatory in the 16:9 cut:
#  (1) the PROBLEM beat after the intro
#      and before the CLI loop;
#  (2) at least one revision —
#      a second CLI → CODE → better
#      OUTPUT cycle;
#  (3) the SUMMARY and NEXT STEPS
#      beats before the outro.
#
# A 16:9 CLI video missing any of
# these is not done.

beats.role_note: SkillTeardownMechanism — the REVISION LAW quoted from SKILL.md §'THE REVISION LAW'
beats.narration_text: Read it in the file's own words. THE REVISION LAW. The sixteen-by-nine video always contains at least one revision cycle. The one exception is the shorts cut. To fit the three-minute cap it ships a single cycle and points the viewer to the sixteen-by-nine for the complete example. The doctrine names its own edge case in the same paragraph.

props.heading: The Revision Law.
props.body: The 16:9 cut always ships with a check-and-change. The 9:16 short is the ONE exception — a single cycle, then a pointer to the long cut.

beats.role_note: ClaudeComposerAsk — the REQUIRED revision. Adds --tool codex to demonstrate the skin swap.
beats.narration_text: The revision. c-l-i, the concept, dash-dash-tool codex. One flag. The same spine renders through the Codex composer instead of Claude's. The body logic and the bookends don't move. The interface skin does. Nothing in the beat sheet has to be rewritten.

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the actual verbatim mapping from SKILL.md 'Converting a sheet between skins'
beats.narration_text: This is how the skin swap is written in the file. A one-to-one rename. ClaudeComposerAsk becomes CodexComposerAsk. ClaudeCodeBeat becomes CodexCodeBeat. ClaudeTitleOutro becomes CodexTitleOutro. Props carry over — same greeting, same command, same title. It is a substitution. Not a re-authoring.

show.event: code card fades in; filename reads 'SKILL.md § skins'
each rename line reveals in narration order

beats.act: DESIGN TELL — the spine survives the skin
beats.narration_text: Here is the design decision I keep coming back to. The skill separates the interface skin — Claude, Codex, Onda, GitHub, Shell — from the narrative spine. Choose a new tool. The same lesson still teaches. That is the thing the file gets right. The spine survives the skin.

props.heading: The spine survives the skin.
props.body: Five interface skins share ONE narrative spine. The body logic and the bookends are IDENTICAL for every tool; only the skin of the input beats changes.
props.quote: The body logic and the bookends above are IDENTICAL for every tool; they differ only in the interface skin of the input beats.
props.verdictLabel: This is the thing the file gets right.

beats.role_note: ClaudeVerdictArtifact — the summary, the artifact page
beats.narration_text: The verdict. c-l-i-dash-explainer is instructions, not software. It reads like an editorial style guide because that is what it is. It doesn't record your terminal — it commissions a reel about what you asked Claude for. Reading the file beats watching a tutorial.

show.event: three artifact lines stagger in, one per spoken claim

artifactLines: Instructions, not software — 365 lines of markdown Claude reads before drafting the reel; there is no compiled binary, no daemon, no service.
The narrative spine is locked in every reel it produces (intro · problem · ask · code · output · revision · summary · handoff · outro); the skin is a --tool flag.
A CLI reel without a check-and-change is incomplete in 16:9 — the doctrine names its own edge case (the shorts cut) in the same paragraph.
It ships as a folder: SKILL.md plus reference/example-cli-beat_sheet.json — the file is the instruction, and Claude is the compiler.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — 'Your turn.' greeting, a real paste-ready prompt read aloud
beats.narration_text: Your turn — here is the prompt, read it with me. Use c-l-i-dash-explainer to build a Brutalist reel about the smallest command in my own workflow. Read skills-slash-make-slash-cli-explainer-slash-SKILL-dot-m-d first. Then propose a beat sheet before you draft narration. The bite is the second sentence. You are asking Claude to read the file, not summarize its name. Liam, in for Bear.
